title: Clo 2025.1 Features Highlights (English)
description:
Learn all about the new features in CLO 2025.1!

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
*Key Features*
0:25 Upgraded 3D Pen
1:17 Denim Wet Wash Effect
2:28 Seamless Blocking
*Avatar Updates*
3:49 Soft Body Simulation Improvements
*Rendering Updates*
4:32 3D Topstich Schematic Render
*UI Updates*
5:01 Seamless CLO-SET & CONNECT Experience
5:36 CLO AI Studio
7:00 Flexible ZPAC Save
*Materials Updates*
7:30 Zipper Style
7:51 CLO zFab Kit x CLOFAB
9:02 Open/Add Specific Colorways
*DXF/Grading Updates*
9:25 Set Grade Point
9:53 2D Snapshot | Add Line Options
*2D CAD*
10:25 Export Standard DXF
10:49 Pattern Drafter Improvement
11:20 Extend/Trim to Unfolded Line
11:38 Notch Improvement
12:10 More Updates

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord- 

---

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/clo-virtual-fashion-inc-/ 
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/clo3d/
transcript: Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here and we have some amazing new features in Chlo that will help you be more productive and creative at the same time. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn all about this new 2025.1 release. Drawing on the avatar using our 3D pen tool allows for you to create ideas within Chlo, even without pattern knowledge. With this update, we have expanded the tool to allow you to create garments that have volume within them. Instead of only drawing directly on the avatar, simply use the shortcut P and start drawing off the avatar. All of the other great shortcuts will still be available to you along with some new ones, like adding a circle around the avatar or showing the distance from your point to the avatar. Ok? Thank you for watching! And, if you enjoyed this video, please consider subscribing to our channel for more And before you know it, you will have drawn a garment within Clow. Using the flattening tool to translate these lines into patterns, Clow will then sew and arrange the patterns on for you. Start adding fabrics and just like that, you have a garment. The tedious work of creating washes is over. Now within Clow, there are eight different denim wash presets for you to adjust and test out within Clow. Unwashed, Rinse, Enzyme, Stone, Acid, Bleach, Ozone, and Custom are all the different wash options that you now have access to. Each wash will have different slider options to adjust based on the selected wash. Each wash will have a cycle time option and a seam abrasion option. If you want to use your own wash, the custom option is for you. Here you can add in your own map and use the sliders to adjust the wash accordingly. When adjusting the cycle time option, the longer the time, the lighter the wash will become. For all the wash options, you will also be able to change the colors as well. Create custom, visual, realistic-looking denim within minutes that will wow all. Ever wanted to test out different textures and colors within the pattern without going through the work of cutting and sewing the pattern pieces? Now you can. This feature was specifically designed to help out all our knitwear designers and get closer to designing and creating seamless garments within Clow. With a multitude of different workflows to create these new seamless blocking lines, the options are endless for creating seamless garments. The tracing tool will trace out internal baselines to seamless lines. Edit pattern tool will allow you to offset as a seamless line. Finally, the seamless line tool itself will allow you to create seamless lines on your patterns. Going into the object browser, you can either assign the fabric or drag and drop it onto the pattern. You will also have the ability to adjust the lines you create in using the edit or transform pattern tools. You can also adjust the texture within each seamless block panel through the edit texture tool, both individually or collectively. By the end, I can create a much more interesting garment quickly and easily, all without cutting a single pattern. Now that's what I call seamless. Now you can apply Softbody to non-skeleton OBJs. There's a whole new world of options like pillows or foam. You can see here when turning on the Softbody, the shape of the avatar actually adjusts and changes due to the fabric. This improvement could also be applied to trims like shoulder pads. Bringing in these as an OBJ, I can apply the Softbody effect to them and now a foam-like effect is applied. Using the slider, I can control the softness amount. Improving the realism of the garments created within Clip. We have updated our schematic render option for topstitches to make a more sketch-like feel to help support techpacks better. Within the topstitch property editor, you can turn on the option of schematic scale and start to edit different visual options like length, spacing, offset, thickness, width, and distance. Making the topstitches much easier to view and see within the schematic render. In Clo, we have updated our library further. The new library is still in the upper right-hand corner, but now when you open it, you will see an entire new tab just for Connect. Within this tab, you will be able to view all your purchases along with all of the great assets that are within the website. Using the filter option, you can filter through all of the events, available assets within Connect, and narrow down on what you are specifically looking for. We have also improved our layout of Closet within the new library to mimic our Closet layout, making it easier to navigate and find your projects. All our generative AI features can now be found within the AI button next to the library for easier access to our AI suite. The process and steps to use these AI features have not been changed. Here, I will use the AI Render Enhancer. As an example, just as before, I can upload a rendered image into my workspace. Using the prompts section, I can cycle through different AI faces by either writing in or auto-generating random prompts. Once a face is chosen, you can preview this and even continue to refine the image using our updated refinement options to get an even more realistic looking face. The new background option from our last review release can also be found here. I can bring in an image and preview it, or I can ask Closet to generate a background and preview those options. Once happy with the result, I can save out these images and use them anywhere. From 2025.1 and onward, by default, all AI features will be deactivated. If you wish to use AI, you will need to activate it manually. For individual users, this can be found through your My Page. For enterprise users, this can be found through your Account Page. You will now have the option to save out selected patterns and trims as a garment, making it easier to take separate parts of a project file and add them into other project files. Like here, I would like to add this across bag into another project file I have. Now with this feature, I can easily do this and create a complete outfit quickly. We have added a zipper tab within our object browser, allowing you to now save out a trim as a whole option and also apply trims quickly and easily within your workspace. You will be able to edit and adjust parts of the zipper individually still and also edit it as a whole, all within the property editor. We have combined the fabric creator with our seamless texture generator to become one CloFab. This will also connect to our new ZFab kit available for pre-order now. Within CloFab, you can create your fabric information at the very top and then go into our map section and bring in your PVR maps. Using the same process as our seamless texture generator, you can then start to create a seamless repeat, either using Clo's help or manually. Once you have the repeat you like, you can then move into the physical properties and follow the same process as the fabric creator. Add in the fabric type, composition, and weight and then see the drape change in real time. Once happy with your fabric physics and visuals, you can then save this out as one ZFab with all the textures and physical properties combined. This can then be brought into your object browser and applied to your garment like so. Now when adding a project or garment, you will be able to choose which colorways to add. If there are less colorways in the current file, Clo will simply add the first colorway to the remaining, allowing you to add and adjust the additional colorways. Let's see how that looks like. Grading within Clo has never been easier. Now within Clo you can choose which points should or shouldn't be graded. Through the right click option, either convert to a non-graded point or graded point. If the point becomes non-graded, then it will follow the grading rules of the graded point closest to it. This will also apply to curve points. We hope this makes grading easier for everyone within Clo. Within 2025.1, we have updated our plotter snapshot options further. Adding in the ability to color code the lines along with applying different line styles, we hope this will increase the usability of the plotter files themselves to more than just printing and maybe even cutting machines, making production within Clo more achievable. Now within Clo you can export and import standard DXFs, allowing for more DXF options and more interoperability within other CAD softwares. Within the DXF export or import popup, in the dropdown menu, there will now be a DXF option. This will be for standard or classic DXF files. Our pattern drafter has expanded, with its AI capabilities, to now be able to read any image, not just a sketch outline. Now you can drop in a picture of a garment you like, and then the pattern drafter will draft a pattern from that image alone. As you can see here. You of course can keep editing it around using the measurements, and once happy, you can select create, and then the garment will automatically be arranged and sewn on the avatar for you. A really nice improvement we have made to our 2D CAD tools is the ability to now extend to the half-symmetric line on half-symmetrical patterns, making it so you no longer have to deal with the duplicate internal lines, making editing internal lines even easier. We have increased our notch options in 2025.1. Our property editor now has more dropdown options for the notch placement. And we have also updated visual options within the user settings for notches. This will help with standardizing how all users across a company view notches. We also hope these improvements to our notch applications and visuals will elevate our software to be more production accurate, and ready. The features you have seen here are just some of the updates we have added in for our 2025.1 release. There are many more as you can see. So check out our manual or our deep dive videos and learn more about all of the features you have seen here. Thank you all so much for watching. I hope you enjoyed learning all of our updates for 2025.1, and enjoyed using Qlo as much as we enjoyed working on it. If you want to learn more about each of these new features, check out the deep dive playlist on our YouTube channel. Don't forget to like and subscribe, thanks again, and keep having fun in Qlo.
markdown_content: ## 3D Pen Tool Enhancements for Garment Creation This section covers the expanded capabilities of Clo's 3D pen tool, including new shortcuts and volumetric garment design features that enable users to create garments directly on or off the avatar without requiring pattern knowledge. Drawing on the avatar using the 3D pen tool now allows creation of garments with volume, not just flat designs. By pressing the shortcut **P**, users can draw off the avatar, expanding creative freedom. Existing shortcuts remain functional, with new additions such as: - Drawing a circle around the avatar. - Displaying the distance from the drawing point to the avatar. Once the garment lines are drawn, the **flattening tool** translates these lines into pattern pieces. Clo automatically sews and arranges these patterns onto the avatar, enabling users to add fabrics and visualize the garment immediately. This workflow streamlines the transition from concept sketches to 3D garments. --- ## Denim Wash Presets and Customization This section details the eight new denim wash presets in Clo 2025.1, including adjustable parameters for cycle time, seam abrasion, and color customization, enabling realistic and customizable denim effects. Clo introduces eight preset denim washes: - Unwashed - Rinse - Enzyme - Stone - Acid - Bleach - Ozone - Custom Each preset includes slider options unique to the wash type, such as: - **Cycle time:** Longer times lighten the wash. - **Seam abrasion:** Adjusts wear around seams. The **Custom** wash option allows users to import their own maps and modify sliders to create personalized washes. Additionally, colors can be changed across all wash types, enabling the creation of realistic, visually rich denim textures within minutes. --- ## Seamless Garment Design and Blocking Lines This section explains Clo's new seamless garment design features, including blocking lines, internal baselines tracing, and texture adjustments, facilitating knitwear and seamless garment workflows without pattern cutting. Designed primarily for knitwear designers, Clo 2025.1 introduces multiple methods to create seamless blocking lines: - **Tracing Tool:** Automatically traces internal baselines as seamless lines. - **Edit Pattern Tool:** Allows offsetting lines to seamless lines. - **Seamless Line Tool:** Enables manual creation of seamless lines on patterns. Within the **Object Browser**, fabrics can be assigned or dragged onto pattern pieces. Seamless block panels’ textures can be adjusted individually or collectively using the **Edit Texture Tool**. This enables quick creation of complex garments without cutting or sewing individual pattern pieces, significantly accelerating the design process. --- ## Softbody Application on Non-Skeleton OBJs This section describes the new ability to apply Softbody physics to non-skeleton objects (OBJs), enhancing realism for accessories and trims such as pillows and shoulder pads. Clo 2025.1 allows Softbody simulation on OBJs without skeleton rigs, opening possibilities for realistic fabric behaviors on items like: - Pillows - Foam trims (e.g., shoulder pads) Users can enable Softbody effects on imported OBJs, with adjustable softness controlled via sliders. The avatar shape dynamically responds to these soft objects, improving garment realism and fitting simulations. --- ## Updated Schematic Render for Topstitches This section highlights improvements to the schematic render mode for topstitches, providing a sketch-like appearance with customizable visual parameters to better support technical pack (techpack) documentation. The topstitch property editor now includes a **schematic scale** option that, when enabled, allows editing of: - Length - Spacing - Offset - Thickness - Width - Distance These settings improve topstitch visibility in schematic renders, making technical details clearer and enhancing communication in techpacks. --- ## New Library Layout and Connect Integration This section outlines updates to Clo’s library interface, including the addition of a Connect tab for asset management and improved Closet layout for easier project navigation. The updated library is located in the upper right corner with a new **Connect** tab that displays: - Purchased assets - Available assets from the Connect website Users can filter assets by event or category for faster searching. The **Closet** layout within the library now mirrors the standalone Closet interface, improving familiarity and navigation efficiency. All generative AI features have been consolidated under an **AI** button next to the library for easier access without changing existing workflows. --- ## AI Render Enhancer and Background Generation This section describes the AI Render Enhancer capabilities for refining facial images and generating or importing backgrounds, along with new user controls for AI feature activation. Users can upload rendered images and use prompts to: - Cycle through AI-generated faces (manual or auto-generated prompts). - Preview and refine faces with enhanced realism using updated options. Backgrounds can be imported as images or generated by Clo’s AI, with preview functionality before finalizing. Starting with version 2025.1, AI features are **disabled by default**; users must manually activate them via: - **My Page** for individual users. - **Account Page** for enterprise users. --- ## Saving Selected Patterns and Trims as Garments This section explains the new ability to save selected patterns and trims as standalone garments, facilitating modular project file management and outfit assembly. Users can now select specific pattern pieces or trims and save them as individual garments. This enables quick reuse and combination of elements across different project files. For example, a bag trim can be saved separately and added to another project, streamlining outfit creation workflows. --- ## Zipper Tab and Trim Management This section covers the new zipper tab in the Object Browser, which simplifies trim management, including saving trims as complete objects and detailed editing within the property editor. The zipper tab allows users to: - Save trims as whole objects. - Quickly apply trims in the workspace. - Edit zipper parts individually or as a whole via the property editor. This enhancement improves trim workflow efficiency and customization. --- ## CloFab: Unified Fabric Creator and Seamless Texture Generator This section introduces CloFab, the combined fabric creation and seamless texture generation tool, integrated with the new ZFab kit, allowing real-time physical property simulation and fabric export. CloFab workflow: 1. Create fabric metadata (name, composition, type). 2. Import PVR maps in the map section. 3. Generate seamless repeats automatically or manually. 4. Adjust physical properties including weight and drape with real-time visualization. 5. Save the fabric as a **ZFab** file, bundling textures and physics. ZFab fabrics can be imported into the Object Browser and applied to garments. The ZFab kit is available for pre-order. --- ## Colorway Management and Grading Improvements This section details enhancements in colorway handling during project import and grading controls for pattern points in Clo 2025.1. When adding projects or garments, users can now select which colorways to include. If the target file has fewer colorways, Clo will replicate the first colorway across missing ones, allowing easier colorway adjustment. Grading has been improved by allowing users to: - Right-click pattern points to toggle between **graded** and **non-graded**. - Non-graded points inherit grading rules from the nearest graded point. - Applies to curve points as well. These updates simplify grading control and accuracy. --- ## Plotter Snapshot Enhancements and DXF Support This section describes new features for plotter snapshots including color-coded lines, line style options, and standard DXF import/export to improve interoperability and production readiness. Plotter snapshot updates: - Ability to color-code lines. - Multiple line style options. These features aim to enhance usability beyond printing, potentially supporting cutting machines and other production tools. Clo now supports importing and exporting **standard (classic) DXF** files via dropdown menus in the DXF dialogs, improving compatibility with other CAD software. --- ## AI-Powered Pattern Drafter Expansion This section explains the AI improvements in Clo's pattern drafter, enabling pattern generation from any garment image, not just sketches. Users can drop any picture of a garment into the pattern drafter, which automatically drafts a pattern based on the image. The pattern remains fully editable with measurement adjustments. Once finalized, users can create the garment, which Clo arranges and sews onto the avatar automatically. --- ## Half-Symmetric Line Extension and Notch Enhancements This section outlines new CAD tool capabilities for half-symmetrical patterns and expanded notch options to improve editing and production accuracy. - The 2D CAD tool now extends to the half-symmetric line on patterns, eliminating duplicate internal lines and simplifying internal line editing. - Notch options in the property editor have expanded dropdown placements. - Visual notch settings in user preferences support standardized notch viewing across teams. These updates contribute to more precise production-ready pattern files. --- # Summary Clo 2025.1 introduces major enhancements in 3D pen volumetric drawing, denim wash presets, seamless garment workflows, Softbody physics on OBJs, schematic render improvements, and a reorganized library with Connect integration. AI features have been centralized with manual activation. Fabric creation has evolved into CloFab with physical simulation and ZFab export. Colorway management, grading controls, plotter snapshot customization, DXF interoperability, and AI-driven pattern drafting improve design efficiency. CAD tools now support half-symmetric line editing and advanced notch options, all aimed at advancing production readiness and user productivity.

chunks.content: Clo now supports importing and exporting **standard (classic) DXF** files via dropdown menus in the DXF dialogs, improving compatibility with other CAD software. --- ## AI-Powered Pattern Drafter Expansion This section explains the AI improvements in Clo's pattern drafter, enabling pattern generation from any garment image, not just sketches. Users can drop any picture of a garment into the pattern drafter, which automatically drafts a pattern based on the image. The pattern remains fully editable with measurement adjustments. Once finalized, users can create the garment, which Clo arranges and sews onto the avatar automatically. --- ## Half-Symmetric Line Extension and Notch Enhancements This section outlines new CAD tool capabilities for half-symmetrical patterns and expanded notch options to improve editing and production accuracy. - The 2D CAD tool now extends to the half-symmetric line on patterns, eliminating duplicate internal lines and simplifying internal line editing. - Notch options in the property editor have expanded dropdown placements. - Visual notch settings in user preferences support standardized notch viewing across teams. These updates contribute to more precise production-ready pattern files. --- # Summary Clo 2025.1 introduces major enhancements in 3D pen volumetric drawing, denim wash presets, seamless garment workflows, Softbody physics on OBJs, schematic render improvements, and a reorganized library with Connect integration. AI features have been centralized with manual activation. Fabric creation has evolved into CloFab with physical simulation and ZFab export. Colorway management, grading controls, plotter snapshot customization, DXF interoperability, and AI-driven pattern drafting improve design efficiency. CAD tools now support half-symmetric line editing and advanced notch options, all aimed at advancing production readiness and user productivity.
